ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a 2-input multiplexer labeled “Multiplexer”; the two data inputs on the left are labeled 0 and 1 respectively, there is a select terminal S at the bottom, and the output on the right is labeled Q. The wire of output Q leads out from the right side and then loops back to connect to the input terminal labeled 0; the input terminal labeled 1 is connected to an external data line; the S terminal is connected to an external control/select line. Reasoning: The output relation of a 2-input MUX can be written as Q_next = (~S)I0 + S I1. From the connections in the figure, I0 = Q_current and I1 = D. Therefore Q_next = (~S)Q_current + S D. When S = 0, Q_next = Q_current, and the circuit holds its original state; when S = 1, Q_next = D, and the output follows the data input. This is exactly the function of a level-sensitive D latch with an enable terminal.

raw_record.question_text: The output of a 2-input multiplexer is connected back to one of its inputs as shown in the figure. This circuit is functionally equivalent to what device?

method.method_draft: First describe the image wiring: the multiplexer output Q is fed back to the 0 input, the 1 input is an external data line, and S is the select line. Apply the 2-input MUX equation Q_next = (~S)I0 + S I1. Substitute I0 = Q_current and I1 = D to get Q_next = (~S)Q_current + S D. Interpret this equation: when S=0 the output remains its old value, and when S=1 the output follows D. Conclude that the circuit is functionally a D latch.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: Q is looped back to one MUX input, so selecting that input recirculates the current output; the other MUX input is an external data input, and S chooses between them. Analyze the two possible select states. If S selects the feedback input 0, the circuit repeatedly sends Q back to itself, so it stores/holds its state. If S selects the external input 1, the output becomes the external data value, so the circuit is transparent to D. A device with a hold mode and a data-load/transparent mode controlled by an enable is a D latch.
